_note: Milestone cards for the mosaic. era=history|recent. 'short' goes on the tiny tile (keep <= 22 chars); 'text' goes on the tap card. Every entry has a source; spot-check before the demo.

headlines.name: Ada Lovelace
headlines.text: Ada Lovelace publishes what is widely considered the first computer program, written for Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine.

headlines.name: Elizabeth Blackwell
headlines.text: Elizabeth Blackwell becomes the first woman to earn a medical degree in the United States.

headlines.name: Victoria Woodhull
headlines.text: Victoria Woodhull becomes the first woman to run for President of the United States.

headlines.name: New Zealand
headlines.text: New Zealand becomes the first self-governing country to grant women the right to vote in national elections.

headlines.name: Marie Curie
headlines.text: Marie Curie becomes the first woman to win a Nobel Prize (Physics). In 1911 she becomes the first person to win a second Nobel.

headlines.name: 19th Amendment
headlines.text: The 19th Amendment is ratified, guaranteeing American women the right to vote.

headlines.name: Bessie Coleman
headlines.text: Bessie Coleman becomes the first African American woman to earn a pilot's license.

headlines.name: Amelia Earhart
headlines.text: Amelia Earhart becomes the first woman to fly solo nonstop across the Atlantic Ocean.

headlines.name: Hedy Lamarr
headlines.text: Hedy Lamarr co-patents frequency-hopping technology, a foundation of later wireless communication.

headlines.name: Gerty Cori
headlines.text: Gerty Cori becomes the first American woman to win a Nobel Prize in science.

headlines.name: Rosalind Franklin
headlines.text: Rosalind Franklin's X-ray image 'Photo 51' reveals the helical structure of DNA.

headlines.name: Grace Hopper
headlines.text: Grace Hopper's team creates the A-0 system, one of the first compilers, paving the way for modern programming languages.

headlines.name: Rosa Parks
headlines.text: Rosa Parks refuses to give up her bus seat in Montgomery, sparking the Montgomery bus boycott.

headlines.name: Sirimavo Bandaranaike
headlines.text: Sirimavo Bandaranaike of Sri Lanka becomes the world's first woman prime minister.

headlines.name: Katherine Johnson
headlines.text: Katherine Johnson verifies the orbital calculations for John Glenn's Friendship 7 flight.

headlines.name: Valentina Tereshkova
headlines.text: Valentina Tereshkova becomes the first woman to fly in space.

headlines.name: Dorothy Hodgkin
headlines.text: Dorothy Hodgkin wins the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for determining structures of biochemical molecules like penicillin.

headlines.name: Kathrine Switzer
headlines.text: Kathrine Switzer becomes the first woman to run the Boston Marathon as a registered entrant.

headlines.name: Shirley Chisholm
headlines.text: Shirley Chisholm becomes the first Black woman elected to the US Congress.

headlines.name: Margaret Hamilton
headlines.text: Margaret Hamilton leads the team that wrote the onboard flight software for the Apollo missions.

headlines.name: Title IX
headlines.text: Title IX bans sex discrimination in US education programs, transforming women's sports.

headlines.name: Billie Jean King
headlines.text: Billie Jean King wins the 'Battle of the Sexes' tennis match watched by millions.

headlines.name: Sandra Day O'Connor
headlines.text: Sandra Day O'Connor becomes the first woman to serve on the US Supreme Court.

headlines.name: Sally Ride
headlines.text: Sally Ride becomes the first American woman in space.

headlines.name: Wilma Mankiller
headlines.text: Wilma Mankiller becomes the first woman Principal Chief of the Cherokee Nation.

headlines.name: Benazir Bhutto
headlines.text: Benazir Bhutto becomes the first woman to lead a Muslim-majority country.

headlines.name: Mae Jemison
headlines.text: Mae Jemison becomes the first African American woman to travel to space.

headlines.name: Toni Morrison
headlines.text: Toni Morrison becomes the first Black woman to win the Nobel Prize in Literature.

headlines.name: Kalpana Chawla
headlines.text: Kalpana Chawla becomes the first Indian-born woman to go to space.

headlines.name: Wangari Maathai
headlines.text: Wangari Maathai becomes the first African woman to win the Nobel Peace Prize.

headlines.name: Elinor Ostrom
headlines.text: Elinor Ostrom becomes the first woman to win the Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences.

headlines.name: Maryam Mirzakhani
headlines.text: Maryam Mirzakhani becomes the first woman to win the Fields Medal, mathematics' highest honor.

headlines.name: Malala Yousafzai
headlines.text: Malala Yousafzai becomes the youngest-ever Nobel laureate for her fight for girls' education.

headlines.name: Donna Strickland
headlines.text: Donna Strickland wins the Nobel Prize in Physics for her work on high-intensity laser pulses.

headlines.name: Christina Koch & Jessica Meir
headlines.text: Christina Koch and Jessica Meir complete the first all-woman spacewalk.

headlines.name: Jennifer Doudna & Emmanuelle Charpentier
headlines.text: Jennifer Doudna and Emmanuelle Charpentier win the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for developing CRISPR gene editing.

headlines.name: Andrea Ghez
headlines.text: Andrea Ghez wins the Nobel Prize in Physics for discovering the supermassive black hole at our galaxy's center.

headlines.name: Kamala Harris
headlines.text: Kamala Harris becomes the first woman Vice President of the United States.

headlines.name: Claudia Goldin
headlines.text: Claudia Goldin becomes the first woman to win the Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences on her own, for research on women's labor market outcomes.

headlines.name: Katalin Karikó
headlines.text: Katalin Karikó shares the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for the mRNA discoveries behind COVID-19 vaccines.

headlines.name: Anne L'Huillier
headlines.text: Anne L'Huillier wins the Nobel Prize in Physics for attosecond light pulses, only the fifth woman to win it.

headlines.name: Narges Mohammadi
headlines.text: Narges Mohammadi wins the Nobel Peace Prize for her fight for women's rights in Iran.

headlines.name: Han Kang
headlines.text: Han Kang becomes the first South Korean writer and first Asian woman to win the Nobel Prize in Literature.

headlines.name: Claudia Sheinbaum
headlines.text: Claudia Sheinbaum, a climate scientist, is elected Mexico's first woman president.

headlines.name: Caitlin Clark
headlines.text: Caitlin Clark becomes NCAA Division I basketball's all-time leading scorer, men's or women's.

headlines.name: Paris Olympics
headlines.text: Paris 2024 becomes the first Olympic Games with an equal number of quota places for women and men.

headlines.name: Sarah Gillis
headlines.text: SpaceX engineer Sarah Gillis performs one of the first commercial spacewalks on Polaris Dawn.

headlines.name: Kirsty Coventry
headlines.text: Kirsty Coventry is elected the first woman, and first African, president of the International Olympic Committee.

headlines.name: Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah
headlines.text: Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah is sworn in as Namibia's first woman president.

headlines.name: Blue Origin NS-31
headlines.text: NS-31 flies the first all-woman crew to space since Valentina Tereshkova's solo flight in 1963.

headlines.name: Mary E. Brunkow
headlines.text: Mary E. Brunkow shares the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discoveries about how the immune system is kept in check.

headlines.name: María Corina Machado
headlines.text: María Corina Machado wins the Nobel Peace Prize for her work promoting democratic rights in Venezuela.

headlines.name: Sanae Takaichi
headlines.text: Sanae Takaichi is elected Japan's first woman prime minister.

headlines.name: Christina Koch
headlines.text: On Artemis II, Christina Koch becomes the first woman to travel around the Moon.

headlines.name: Keisha Lance Bottoms
headlines.text: Keisha Lance Bottoms wins election as Georgia's first woman governor.

headlines.name: Marsha Blackburn
headlines.text: Marsha Blackburn wins election as Tennessee's first woman governor.
